goal:
In kestrel-team (Python; gate `uv run --locked python -m pytest tests/ -q`,
fully mocked, no network; main 025c423, release 0.3.0), add two things the
tenant trigger practice-helm decisions/0003 names (Accepted 2026-10-21;
kestrel-helm decisions/0033 adopts the seat side): (A) a decision-record
contract document and (B) six helm checks under `spawner doctor`. Nothing
else changes; 0025 decision 2 freezes the loop's capability and this touches
no executor, no routing, no ledger. READ CLAUDE.md FIRST.

(A) `docs/decision_record_contract.md`, beside `docs/queue_item_contract.md`
and in its shape (purpose, where records live, item shape, a fields table,
what is refused). The contract: a record is `decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md` with
YAML frontmatter of exactly five fields — `kind: ruling | capability`,
`status: proposed | accepted | superseded`, `ruled: <ISO date>`,
`enforced_by: [<path or command>, ...]`, `supersedes: [<NNNN>, ...]`. Rules:
a `capability` record may be `accepted` only when `enforced_by` is non-empty
and every entry resolves (a path exists relative to the helm, or a command
exits 0); a `ruling` carries `enforced_by: []`; `accepted` records are never
edited, only superseded (a later record lists them in `supersedes`). Records
without frontmatter are legal and reported as `legacy`, never refused: the
49 accepted records that predate the contract are triaged by the check, not
broken by it. Source of the wording: practice-helm decisions/0003 decision 2,
quoted in context_pointers.

(B) `kestrel_team/core/helm_checks.py`: `helm_checks(manifest) ->
List[Dict]` returning rows in `introspect.environment_checks()`'s shape
`{name, ok, detail}` (ok=None informational), one row per check, for the
helm the active manifest names (`InstanceManifest` in `core/instance.py`:
`intent_plane`, `queue_dir`, `ledger_root`, `peers()`, the repo set). The
six checks, named exactly: (1) `manifest-settings`: every repo in the
manifest's `repos:` resolves to a path in `<intent_plane>/.claude/settings.json`
`permissions.additionalDirectories`, and every additionalDirectories entry
is in `repos:` or `peers:` — report each unmatched side in `detail`;
(2) `queue-parses`: `queue_items.load_queue(<queue_dir>)` raises nothing
(reuse it; do not re-implement the parser); (3) `sandbox-present`:
settings.json has `sandbox.enabled: true`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands:
false`, and `filesystem.allowWrite` contains the manifest's `ledger_root`
(compare after `~` expansion); (4) `no-placeholders`: no tracked file under
the helm contains `{{` (walk the tree, skip `.git`) — the sentinel is the
module constant `PLACEHOLDER = "{{"` in helm_checks.py, written exactly once
and the only `{{` in that file (no docstring, comment or f-string escape
contains it, so the mutation below can only hit code); (5) `rulings-contract`:
every file under `<intent_plane>/decisions/` matching `NNNN-*.md` is parsed
with `queue_items._split_frontmatter` (reuse it); no frontmatter → counted
`legacy`; with frontmatter → the five fields present with legal values, and
an `accepted` `capability` has non-empty `enforced_by` whose entries resolve
(path exists under the helm, or command exits 0 with `cwd=intent_plane`,
10-second timeout); `detail` names every failing record; (6) `claude-md`:
`<intent_plane>/CLAUDE.md` is at most 60 lines and every relative markdown
link in it (`[..](path)`) resolves to an existing file. `ok` is False on any
failure, with the failing items named; the function never raises.

Wire it: `spawner doctor` gains `--helm` (flag; default off so existing
output is byte-identical without it): with the flag, after the Environment
block, print a "Helm checks (<instance name>):" block via
`introspect.render_environment_checks(helm_checks(manifest))`, and exit
nonzero if any check's ok is False. No manifest set → the block says so and
ok=None. Tests: `tests/test_helm_checks.py`, fixtures built in `tmp_path`
(a minimal helm: manifest, settings.json, queue/, decisions/, CLAUDE.md),
one passing case and one failing case per check, plus a `legacy` record
case and an `accepted capability` whose `enforced_by` command exits 1.
The mutation above (turning `PLACEHOLDER = "{{"` into `"%%"`) must fail at least
one test. Update `docs/capabilities.md` with one line per new check and
`CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased.

(C) Amended 2026-10-21 from the seat (practice-helm decisions/0006, the two
ladders, Proposed): the work ladder's top rungs become queue fields. In
`docs/queue_item_contract.md` and `core/queue_items.py` `_validate` (line
359), two optional fields: `merged: <sha>` — a 7-to-40 hex string, refused
(`malformed`, like any bad field) if present and not hex; `verified: <str>`
— a CI run URL or a verifier exit line, refused if present and empty, and
refused if present without `merged`. Neither changes `STATUSES` or any
drain transition; they are read by `doctor` and by the seat brief, never by
the drain. `set_item_status` is untouched. In the decision record contract
(A), one paragraph names the two knowledge rungs below `ruling`:
`observation` (a dated sentence in a queue Record) and `finding` (dated,
with the command and its quoted output, shape `Finding (YYYY-MM-DD): <claim>
— <command> → <output>`), neither of which is a record and neither of which
the parser reads. A seventh helm check, `ladder-fields`: every queue item's
`merged`/`verified` satisfy the rules above (the drain refuses a malformed
item outright; this check reports which, so `doctor` is useful on a helm
the drain would refuse). Tests for both refusals and the seventh check in
the same test files.
